Quick reference guide

Purpose. Use this explorer to generalize OLS projection from a line to the predictor subspace span(x1c,x2c).

Controls / options

ItemMeaningHow to read it
true β₁, β₂Data-generating slopes.Set the signal carried by each predictor.
corr(x₁,x₂)Predictor correlation.High |correlation| creates multicollinearity and makes coefficient estimates unstable.
noise σNoise level.Raises residual variation.
sample sizeNumber of observations.Larger samples stabilize the fitted plane.
highlightSelects an observation.Highlights it in predictor and observed-vs-fitted plots.
yaw / pitchCamera orientation for the projection panel.Changes display only.
generate new sampleResamples the synthetic dataset.Shows sampling variability.

Charts

ItemMeaningHow to read it
Predictor scatterx₂ versus x₁.An elongated cloud signals predictor collinearity.
Projection onto predictor planeyc decomposed into ŷc in span(x1c,x2c) plus perpendicular residual e.This is the geometric meaning of the normal equations.
Observed vs fittedy versus ŷ.Points near the diagonal are well predicted.
SST/SSR/SSEVariance decomposition.The same Pythagorean decomposition extends to multiple regression.

Metrics

ItemMeaningHow to read it
α̂, β̂₁, β̂₂OLS coefficient estimates.Interpret conditionally: each slope is the partial effect holding the other predictor fixed.
sample corr(x₁,x₂)Predictor dependence.Large magnitude warns of collinearity.
R²Fraction of centered response sum of squares explained by the predictor subspace.Equals squared cosine of the angle from yc to its projection.
x₁c·e, x₂c·eNormal-equation orthogonality checks.Should be approximately zero.
det(X'X) indicatorDeterminant of the centered 2×2 Gram matrix.Small values signal near-linear dependence.

Core mathematical identity

β̂=(XcᵀXc)⁻¹Xcᵀyc, ŷc=P_X yc, P_X=Xc(XcᵀXc)⁻¹Xcᵀ.

Quick reference guide

Purpose. Use this explorer to study the bias–variance tradeoff by fitting polynomial models of different complexity to noisy samples from a fixed nonlinear function.

Controls / options

ItemMeaningHow to read it
polynomial degreeModel complexity.Low degree tends to underfit; high degree can become unstable.
noise σIrreducible observation noise.Raises the noise floor of achievable prediction error.
sample sizeTraining observations.More data usually reduces variance.
evaluation x₀Location where bias and variance are estimated over repeated samples.Edge regions often exhibit more variance.
resampleCreates a fresh displayed training sample.The Monte Carlo bias/variance calculation still averages over many samples.

Charts

ItemMeaningHow to read it
Data + fitted polynomialOne training sample, true function and current fitted polynomial.Compare systematic misspecification versus oscillatory overfitting.
Bias–variance decompositionBias², model variance and noise variance at x₀.Expected prediction error is approximately bias²+variance+noise.

Metrics

ItemMeaningHow to read it
Train MSEAverage squared residual on the displayed training set.Usually falls as degree rises.
Test-grid MSESquared error against the noiseless true function on a dense grid.Shows generalization of the mean function.
Bias² at x₀Squared difference between average fitted prediction and true f(x₀).Captures systematic model error.
Variance at x₀Variance of fitted predictions across repeated training samples.Captures sensitivity to sample fluctuations.
Noise σ²Irreducible variance.Cannot be removed by model choice.

Core mathematical identity

E[(Y−f̂(x))²] = Bias[f̂(x)]² + Var[f̂(x)] + σ² under the standard regression decomposition.

Quick reference guide

Purpose. Use this explorer to interpret Bayesian linear regression as the multiplication of a Gaussian prior by a Gaussian likelihood, producing a Gaussian posterior over coefficients and a posterior predictive distribution.

Controls / options

ItemMeaningHow to read it
true slope βSlope used to generate synthetic data.Changes the data-generating relationship.
noise σKnown observation-noise standard deviation used by the Bayesian model.Wider noise makes the likelihood and posterior less concentrated.
prior scale τStandard deviation of the zero-mean isotropic Gaussian prior on (α,β).Small τ produces stronger shrinkage toward zero.
sample sizeNumber of observations.More data makes the likelihood dominate the prior.
prediction x₀Point where posterior predictive uncertainty is reported.Uncertainty tends to grow away from the center of observed x values.
resampleGenerates a new dataset.Shows posterior sampling sensitivity.

Charts

ItemMeaningHow to read it
Coefficient posterior geometryPrior, likelihood/OLS, and posterior ellipses in (α,β) space.The posterior is a precision-weighted compromise between prior and likelihood.
Posterior predictive regressionData, posterior mean line, and approximate 95% predictive band.Band includes coefficient uncertainty plus observation noise.

Metrics

ItemMeaningHow to read it
Posterior α, βPosterior means.Bayesian point estimates under squared-error loss.
Posterior SDsMarginal posterior standard deviations.Quantify coefficient uncertainty.
95% credible intervalsMean ±1.96 SD for each marginal Gaussian posterior.Posterior probability statement conditional on the model.
Shrinkage βPosterior slope relative to OLS.Shows prior influence.
Predictive SD at x₀sqrt(σ² + x₀*ᵀΣpost x₀*).Includes future observation noise and parameter uncertainty.

Core mathematical identity

Σpost=(XᵀX/σ²+I/τ²)⁻¹, μpost=Σpost Xᵀy/σ², and y*|x*,D is Gaussian with variance σ²+x*ᵀΣpost x*.
